trait WriteStream extends { Closeable }

    (** %write(FlatString)% and %write(Char)% are the primitive mechanisms
        for writing characters to  a %WriteStream%. **)

    abstract write(s: String):()
    abstract write(c: Char):()

    (** %write(Any)% converts its argument to a String using %asString%
        and appends the result to the stream. **)
    write(x: Any):() =
            typecase x of
                x':Object ⇒ write x'.asString
                else   ⇒ write ("" || x)                   (* handles tuples *)
            end

    (** %writes% converts each of the generated elements to a string
        using %asString% unless the element is already a %String% in
        which case it is left alone.  The resulting strings are
        appended together to the end of the stream.  To avoid
        interleaving with concurrent output to the same stream, this
        append step is done monolithically. **)
    writes(x:Generator[\Any\]):() = writes(x,"")
    writes(x: Generator[\Any\], rest: String):() =
        write((BIG ||[e ← x]
                   typecase e of
                        e':String ⇒ e'
                        e':Object ⇒ e'.asString
                        else   ⇒ ("" || e)                 (* handles tuples *)
                   end) || rest)

    (** %print% and %println% convert each of their arguments to a
        string using %asString% unless the element is already a
        %String% in which case it is left alone.  The resulting
        strings are appended together monolithically to the end of the
        stream.  The %println% method also appends a newline.  Both
        then flush the stream. *)
    print(args:Any...): () = do writes(args,""); flush() end
    println(args:Any...): () = do writes(args,"\n"); flush() end

    (** %flush% any output to the stream that is still buffered. **)
    abstract flush():()

    abstract close():()

end WriteStream

end Stream

# Rung R, climb batch 28: the skeptic's verdict

Head judged: `9632f4e5f906d1aae8103e1d45ec83a0700c0efc` (the worker's last commit). My commits: `c00f51c2` (a defect, contested), `c7d72a1a` (corrections), then this file. Verdict: **contested**, with one contested fix.

The journal step wrote nothing: `REPORT.md` and `record.md` were on the branch (`9632f4e5`). `journal-text.py` wrote both texts to `tmp/rung-io-reader/skeptic/`; each equals the committed file but for its final newline (`cmp: EOF on tmp/rung-io-reader/skeptic/REPORT.journal.md after byte 37710, in line 224`, and the record's `after byte 14425, in line 41`).

## What I checked

1. **The stages.** `tmp/rung-io-reader/checker-count-postedit.txt` against `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/gate/checker-count.txt`: `diff` prints nothing (`#total 0`, `#crash none`). `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-27/gate/distance.txt tmp/rung-io-reader/distance-postedit.txt` prints `DISTANCE SAME   0`; its two crash rows are the gate's (`#crash decl ObjectDecl FortressBuiltin.fss:661:1-773:2 IllegalArgumentException Comparison method violates its general contract!` and `#crash stage component FortressBuiltin leftover`). In the worker's transcript the count started at 04:29:30 (call `3j6qmH`, `git log --oneline -1`: `14be0d36`) and the distance at 04:31:31 (`PADegj`), after its last edit of code (03:37:25, `YzVjo6`, `Library/Reader.fss`) and its build (03:37:53, `g9gVFr`). The report's tables are those of the worker's head; my fixes change `Library/File.fss` and tests, which neither stage reads, and I ran no stage.
2. **Test first.** The walk test was written at 03:32:49 (`Neh3Xd`) and failed through the harness on the base's code at 03:33:25 (`zSkwuv`), before the first edit of a library source (03:36:07, `LQZs8A`): `tree 157323e5`, 'Unification error: Closure/Constructor for writeOn param 1 (stream:WriteStream) got arg <Write handle to "NativeHelperReaderWalk.out"> of type FileWriteStream', 'Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0'. The three copies at 03:33:56, 03:34:07 and 03:34:19 (`tmp/rung-io-reader/harness-base-v1.txt` to `v3`) print 'Cannot find definition for method flush …', 'Performed operation on consumed FileReadStream NativeHelperReaderWalk.out' and 'FileNotFound: no-such-dir-NativeHelperReaderWalk/missing.txt'. The compiled guard failed on the base through `junit.sh` at 03:34:38 ('builtinPrimitive names no static helper: com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.fileOps.jbrStdIn', 'Tests run: 2,  Failures: 2,  Errors: 0'); its final form, changed after the first run on the edit, failed on the old code at 03:42:29 (`tmp/rung-io-reader/junit-old2.txt`, the same refusal). The last runs after the last change of code: the harness at 03:45:15 (`tree 14be0d36`, 'OK (6 tests)') and `junit.sh new2` at 03:41:52 ('OK (6 tests)'), as `recordedPass` quotes. `ant testSystem` (shards 197, 190, 197, 195, 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL') and `ant testQuick` (1451, 86, 263, 'BUILD SUCCESSFUL') ran after it, on `14be0d36` (`tmp/rung-io-reader/testSystem.txt:940`, `testQuick.txt:4268`).
3. **The diff,** line by line, against the section and P-164, P-58, F-330 and F-299. `JavaBufferedReader`'s eight natives and two factories are P-58's form on `fileOps` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1959-1979`); `JavaBufferedReaderObject.java` is rung W's `JavaBufferedWriterObject.java` with the reader's names (a `diff` after `sed s/Writer/Reader/` differs only in a parameter's name); `StaticNativeApp`'s four methods carry the trait as `JavaBufferedWriter` is carried; `jbrStdIn` stands beside `jbwStdErr`; `File` and `Reader` are plain components over a field `under`, with the factories in `Writer(fileName)`'s form. The 25 glue bindings go and 10 helper bindings come: the worker's `countbind.py` prints 'helper 341 glue 102 total 443' on `/home/user/fortress-base28` (`File.fss helper 0 glue 15`, `Reader.fss helper 0 glue 10`) and 'helper 351 glue 77 total 428' on the head. One defect: `FileWriteStream`'s `write(x:String)` (finding 1).

## Findings and fixes

### Finding 1, a defect: `FileWriteStream` writes a rope leaf by leaf, so lines from parallel tasks interleave (contested fix `c00f51c2`)

`Library/File.fss:56` on `9632f4e5`, `write(x:String):() = x.writeOn(self)`: a string that is not flat writes itself one leaf per Java write (`Library/String.fss:163-166`), so at four threads lines from a parallel `for` break apart. `File.fsi`'s `writes` says its append "is done monolithically" so as not to interleave with concurrent output (`Library/File.fsi:111-116`), and `print` and `println` work "much like %writes%" (`:119`, `:122`). Before the rung a rope stopped the run (row 900), so no file was ever broken; the rung's repair of row 900 made the broken lines reachable.

The test, `ProjectFortress/tests/FileWriteStreamParallelWalk.fss`, writes 600 lines past a flat string's size by `write`, `println` and `writes` from parallel `for`s and asserts each line whole. On `9632f4e5`, through the harness, twice:

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-io-reader/skeptic/h-head ProjectFortress/tests/FileWriteStreamParallelWalk.fss

    Tests run: 1,  Failures: 1,  Errors: 0
    (and at 06:25:22, beside the guards: 'FAIL: a ZZ32: 252 =/= a ZZ32: 600; lines written by write from parallel tasks')

The fix: `write(x:String):() = under.write(x)`, `JavaBufferedWriter`'s write over `String`, which flattens and makes one Java write (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1950-1953`), as `Writer`'s `write(s: String)` does (`Library/Writer.fss:32-35`), without its flush. After it, through the harness with the guards:

    explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh $PWD/tmp/rung-io-reader/skeptic/h-fix ProjectFortress/tests/FileWriteStreamParallelWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperReaderWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/NativeHelperWriterWalk.fss ProjectFortress/tests/FileReadWrite.fss ProjectFortress/tests/WordCountSmall.fss ProjectFortress/tests/FileConversion.fss ProjectFortress/tests/LongStringTests.fss ProjectFortress/tests/XXXWriterCharSupplementaryWalk.fss
    . interpret tmp/rung-io-reader/skeptic/h-fix/tests/FileWriteStreamParallelWalk
    every line came back unbroken

# Rung R, climb batch 28: the judge's ruling

Head judged: `1bee165f` on `wip/rung-io-reader`. One contested fix: `c00f51c2`, `FileWriteStream`'s `write(x:String)`. Ruling: **upheld**. Decision: **stands**; no revert, no repair round.

## The fix

`c00f51c2` changes `Library/File.fss:56` on `9632f4e5`, `write(x:String):() = x.writeOn(self)`, into `write(x:String):() = under.write(x)` (now `Library/File.fss:57`), and adds `ProjectFortress/tests/FileWriteStreamParallelWalk.fss`. `JavaBufferedWriter`'s `write(s: String)` flattens by a `typecase` on `asFlatString` and makes one native write (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1949-1952`); that write is one call of `java.io.BufferedWriter.write(String, int, int)` (`compiler/runtimeValues/FortressBufferedWriter.java:47-50`, by `nativeHelpers/fileOps.java:109-111`), so one string reaches the file whole. The fix adds no `flush`; `writes`, `print` and `println` stay the team's text (`Library/File.fss:59-68`).

## What settles it

1. **The api asks for a monolithic append.** `FileWriteStream`'s `writes`: "To avoid interleaving with concurrent output to the same stream, this append step is done monolithically" (`Library/File.fsi:111-116`); `print` and `println` work "much like %writes%" (`:119`, `:122-124`). `writes` reaches `write(x:String)` whenever its joined string is not flat (`Library/File.fss:59-65`), so the leaf-by-leaf `writeOn` (`Library/String.fss:163-166`, `:493-504`) breaks the api's own promise. `WriteStream` says the same of every write stream (`Library/Stream.fss:49-54`, `:64-69`). data.ruling:
Fix c00f51c2 (FileWriteStream's write(x:String) changed from x.writeOn(self) to under.write(x)) is UPHELD. The specification is silent: it names no I/O object, and its only sentence on interleaving is Specification/basic/evaluation/parallelism.tex:90, which is about scheduling. The library's own api settles the point. File.fsi:111-116 says writes' append "is done monolithically" to avoid interleaving, and print and println work "much like writes" (:119, :122-124). writes reaches write(x:String) whenever its joined string is not flat (Library/File.fss:59-65). The leaf-by-leaf writeOn (Library/String.fss:163-166, :493-505) breaks that promise. WriteStream says the same at Library/Stream.fss:49-54 and :64-69. The library's way is to write a rope once. The team's Writer wrapped a rope in a BufferedWriter of size |s| and flushed it, so the rope went out in one write (git show c2178040^:Library/Writer.fss, lines 45-49; the glue buffer is at interpreter/glue/prim/BufferedWriter.java:34-38). Rung W flattens and writes once (Library/Writer.fss:31-35), for the reason in rung-io-writer/REPORT.md:144, decision 7. The team's ConcurrentPrinting.fss states the intent. Fork R2's default also says "its writes, flush and close over under, as Writer's are" (CLIMB-BATCH-28.md:406).

Worker, right: rows 900 and 901 need only WriteStream and flush. The team's FileWriteStream flushes in none of its writes, and the fix keeps that buffering.
Worker, wrong: "the team's text already writes a rope through writeOn" is no evidence. That text never ran on the base, where a rope stopped the run (row 900, REPORT.md:59). Also wrong: reading fork R2 as covering only the primitive writes ignores its "as Writer's are".

Skeptic, right: the measured broken lines ('432 =/= ... 600' and '252 =/= ... 600' through harness-one.sh at four threads on 9632f4e5, then 'OK (8 tests)' after the fix); File.fsi's text; fork R2's words; rung W's decision 7; and that the base could never break a line.
Skeptic, partly right: "as Writer's are" also covers Writer's flush after a rope (Library/Writer.fss:34), which the fix leaves out. File.fsi asks no write to flush (:102-109, :127-128), and the single write is enough for a monolithic append, so the fix stands as it is. The divergence goes to the curator. The write is atomic because it is one call to java.io.BufferedWriter.write (compiler/runtimeValues/FortressBufferedWriter.java:47-50, via fileOps.java:109-111).

Broken lines were measured at 432 and 252 of 600 on 9632f4e5, and the rung's repair of row 900 made them reachable. The fix keeps the worker's buffering by adding no flush.
